author: sonnet
label: climb-04-01
changes: Added a short opening summary of how the gateway works today and what this adds, so a newcomer has context.
Added a Terms section (plan, limit, window, fail open).
Removed all 'req N' references and restated each rule in plain words.
Stated that the Key Service plan is the only source and that the gateway uses its own limit for headers.
Decided that Enterprise requests skip the check while the limit is unset, and recorded it.
Said what the script returns and how the gateway uses it to choose 429 or forward.
Noted that a key without expiry is harmless because the window is in the key name.
Stated that the key cache is per instance and keyed by API key, and that revoked keys can work for up to 5 minutes.
Stated that fail open can add up to 50 ms per request, with no circuit breaker in v1.
Added a line on slow backends (unchanged, out of scope) and an open question about the backend timeout.
Merged the old edge-case lines on staleness and unknown key into the shorter edge-case list, and moved terms and context ahead of the decisions.
Merged the 'Rejected requests cost nothing' and 'Passed requests always count' decisions into one bullet.
Cut the sentence about the gateway keeping its own copy of the limit and the script not returning it; folded it into the Limit by plan bullet in shorter form.
Cut the note about a key left without expiry wasting memory (a detail the main flow does not need).
Merged the separate Edge cases bullets into a single Failure cases list that also covers Redis slow or down and Redis failover, pointing to the Fail open decision instead of repeating it.
Dropped the separate 'window = floor(now/60)' step in the script and folded it into the key line, so the script has four steps.
Shortened the Window and Headers bullets and the Enterprise bullet by removing repeated phrasing.
Trimmed the intro to say plainly how the gateway works today, then what this design adds.
Kept the diagram, terms, decisions, and open questions in the newcomer order; rollout is not covered because the brief asks only for the runtime design.
holes: Q8: What happens if the backend is slow or never answers after the counter was incremented? Does the gateway have a timeout and what does the client see? (author: The brief does not say what backend timeout the gateway has today. The counter stays used regardless. I added a line saying the existing gateway behaviour is unchanged, and an open question.)
